win_claim.quote: achieving the best predictive performance when compared with the traditional SMOTE approach and other recent variants on low- and high-dimensional settings

uncertain: Per-dataset G-mean values are from the Supplementary file Table A.4 (text extraction); bold marks lost, so 'marks' not captured; supplementary page index vs printed p.32 not verified.
Dataset names in supplementary tables are IDs (ldd1..hdd12); mapped to names via Table 1 order, p.7.
Table 1 prints ldd17 class % as (91.7, 8.3) (reversed vs others) and ldd22 as '(4.9.95.1)'; kept as printed.
Table 1 gives only class percentages, no counts: n_minority/n_majority null. For hdd rows column order read as IR, #Att, #Samples (text extraction, p.7).
n_classes=2 inferred from 'binary classification' in Appendix table titles; not a Table 1 column.
ecoli, abalone7, image1, solar, yeast3-5 are natively multiclass/other in UCI/KEEL; how binarized not stated, so how_obtained set to not stated for all.

Metric choice: G-mean per-dataset exists only in supplementary (Table A.4); main-text Tables 2-3 give averages/ranks only. Rank is AUC-based. Classifier: abstract highlights none; k-NN first reported (also best average per text, p.9).
best_other computed as max over baselines excluding SMOTE and FW-SMOTE (includes PCA-S., ties listed).
notes: Proposed = FW-SMOTE (weighted Minkowski/OWA SMOTE variant; parameters r in {n/2,3n/4,n}, p in {1,2,inf}, alpha in {0.4,0.6} grid searched). Other classifiers' per-dataset G-mean in Tables A.5 (SVM) and A.6 (LR), AUC in A.1-A.3 of supplementary. Oversampling amount N=1 or 3 chosen on average test performance. Table 5 (feature selection comparison) not used. No GitHub link for results seen.
